P1: Renamed (Jan 2026 PSA): Player:LoadCharacter -> Player:LoadCharacterAsync; BadgeService:AwardBadge -> BadgeService:AwardBadgeAsync; MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo -> MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync. Instance:WaitForChild and RemoteFunction:InvokeServer (also InvokeClient, BindableFunction:Invoke) were NOT renamed and remain current. The old names still work: they are deprecated informationally only (same behaviour, no removal scheduled), so use the Async names in new code. Minor caveat: very old mobile client builds briefly lacked some Async names, only relevant for client code.
P2: Workspace > Server Authority: set Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server. This forces NextGenerationReplication, PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem, StreamingEnabled and UseFixedSimulation to Enabled and SignalBehavior to Deferred. Client-predicted gameplay logic goes in a function registered with RunService:BindToSimulation; it must be deterministic (no Destroy/reparenting/EquipTool, no UserInputService - read input from InputAction), with predicted state in attributes (first 64 replicate, names/strings up to 50 chars). Use the time() clock inside it - tick(), os.time() and os.clock() do not roll back on resimulation. Rendering, sounds and VFX go in RenderStepped and must tolerate mispredictions.
P3: Property: Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem. Timeline: June 2026 opt-in (default Disabled); early 2027 default becomes Enabled (planned); mid 2027 the property is removed and the legacy player scripts are gone (planned). At risk: code that calls PlayerModule internals such as require(PlayerModule):GetControls() (Enable/Disable controls), code relying on the old ContextActionService input sinking/priority behaviour of default controls, and forked/custom copies of PlayerModule/ControlModule (those need StarterPlayer.CreateDefaultPlayerModule = Disabled with the property Enabled, or must be ported).
P4: It introduced platform-integrated chat (TextChatService.PlatformIntegratedChat). When enabled, message text is no longer exposed to game code: TextChatMessage.Text and .Translation return an empty string (with a warning), OnIncomingMessage and Player.Chatted no longer give the text, custom chat UIs cannot draw messages (prototype with TextChannelWindow), TextChannel:SendAsync from game code is replaced by Quick Words, and admin commands should use TextChatCommand. Timeline: opt-in (Studio) from October 2026 until February 2027; on by default with opt-out in February 2027; mandatory by May 2027. Don't build new features that read chat text (keyword triggers, chat minigames, filters).
P5: Since July 29 2026 limits are per experience (shared by all servers and Open Cloud), per request type per minute, scaled by concurrent users: Read = 300 + 40 x CCU; Write = 300 + 20 x CCU; List = 300 + 2 x CCU; Remove = 300 + 40 x CCU. UpdateAsync consumes one Read plus one Write. Per key there is a 4 MB/min write throughput limit. Storage limit: 500 MB + 1 MB per lifetime player. Open Cloud scripts drain the same budget, so self-throttle with DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType and keep headroom.
P6: Because Gems can be bought with Robux, crates opened with Gems are paid random items. Before purchase you must show every possible outcome with its numeric odds (totals exactly 100%, rounded with disclaimer, no non-zero shown as 0%), reachable through a clearly labelled control. The Luck Potion must state its numeric effect before purchase, and while active the displayed odds must update to the player's actual boosted odds. Per player, on the server, call PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync and check ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted; if true (or the call fails/key missing - fail closed) don't let them buy/open paid crates (or the potion), offering a compliant alternative such as direct purchase. Enforce in the server purchase path, not just the UI.
P7: Roblox Kids: accounts for ages 5-8, see only experiences rated Minimal or Mild that pass selection; communication is off by default. Roblox Select: ages 9-15, experiences up to Moderate that pass selection. Creator requirements: ID-verified, 2-Step Verification enabled, and an active Roblox Plus subscription. Game requirements: a completed maturity/content questionnaire with a qualifying rating (Minimal/Mild for Kids, up to Moderate for Select) and passing Roblox's selection review; social hangouts and free-form drawing experiences are excluded by default. Check eligibility in the Audience Reach dashboard.
P8: Creator Rewards (since July 2025) pays Earned Robux with a 60-day hold: Daily Engagement pays about 5 Robux per Active Spender per day who plays your experience 10+ minutes when it is among their first experiences that day; Audience Expansion pays 35% of the first $100 spent by new users you bring to Roblox (within 60 days; ID-verified owner, ~100+ average DAU). DevEx: standard rate 0.0038 USD per Earned Robux (since Sept 5 2025; older legacy balances cash out at 0.0035 first). From June 8 2026 a higher 0.0054 USD rate applies to Robux earned from qualifying spend by age-checked US 18+ players. Purchased Robux cannot be exchanged.
G1: Rules: (1) Only one script sets MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt. (2) Look up the player; if absent, return NotProcessedYet. (3) Check the PurchaseId hasn't already been granted (record processed PurchaseIds in the same saved document as the grant, e.g. via UpdateAsync/session-locked profile). (4) Grant and persist successfully, then return PurchaseGranted. (5) On any error, unknown product, or failed save return NotProcessedYet so Roblox retries. Never grant in PromptProductPurchaseFinished, never yield indefinitely. Charged but nothing: the callback returned PurchaseGranted before/despite a failed grant or save (or errored, or a second ProcessReceipt overwrote the handler so the product is never handled). Double items: no idempotency - Roblox retries receipts (rejoin, server crash, NotProcessedYet after a grant that actually succeeded), and without a PurchaseId check stored atomically with the grant the item is given again.
G2: Use UpdateAsync whenever the new value depends on the old one or multiple servers might write the key (player data, counters, receipts, trades): it reads the latest value and retries if another server wrote in between, avoiding clobbering; SetAsync blindly overwrites (fine only for write-once/independent values). Player data should also use a session lock. Transform rules: must not yield (no task.wait, no other Async/DataStore calls, no remote invokes); may run multiple times, so be pure/idempotent and reset any flags on entry - no side effects like granting items or firing remotes inside; return nil to cancel the write; return the new value (plus keyInfo:GetUserIds() and keyInfo:GetMetadata() if you want to keep them, otherwise they are cleared); handle a nil input (new key) explicitly; keep size under limits. Wrap the call in pcall.
G3:
Not safe. typeof(gold) == 'number' still allows NaN (NaN < 0 and NaN > x are both false, so it passes), inf is caught but fractional values like 0.5 pass, and 0 offers pass. Also no check that the player isn't already in a trade/offer spam, and gold isn't reserved, so the player can offer the same gold in many offers or spend it before acceptance (duplication). Fix:
```lua
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
  if typeof(gold) ~= 'number' or gold ~= gold or gold % 1 ~= 0 then return end
  if gold <= 0 or gold > player.Gold.Value then return end
  if pendingOffer[player] or rateLimited(player) then return end
  pendingOffer[player] = gold -- reserve/escrow
  createOffer(player, gold)
end)
```
Re-validate the balance server-side at acceptance and transfer atomically; clear pendingOffer on PlayerRemoving.
G4: The Animator writes Motor6D.Transform every frame during its animation step, after Heartbeat-time scripts in effect, so your Heartbeat write is overwritten by the idle pose (Transform is meant to be owned by the animator). Write procedural offsets in RunService.PreSimulation (formerly Stepped), which runs after animations are applied and before physics/render, and compose rather than compound: keep your own offset and set motor.Transform = aimOffset * baseTransform (not Transform = Transform * offset each frame). Alternatively stop animations from keying that joint. Edit C0 instead only for a static/rarely-changing rest offset (e.g. permanently reorienting a mount on a Motor6D you own), knowing C0 replicates and changes the base the animation plays on; restore it if changed.
G5: Roblox resolves per joint: the highest AnimationPriority track (Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4) that animates that joint wins outright; lower-priority tracks only affect joints the higher one doesn't key. Within the same priority, tracks are blended by weight (weights normalized, e.g. 1 and 0.6 give roughly 60/40). If the swing is at Core/Idle or the same Movement priority as walk, it is averaged with or overridden by walk, so it looks weak. A weight below 1 (or a fade in progress) with nothing beneath blends toward rest. Fix: set the swing track's Priority to Action (or higher) before Play, play at weight 1 (AdjustWeight) with a short fadeTime, and make sure the animation asset itself is saved with that priority.
G6: Blender works in metres while Roblox uses studs; FBX stores unit scale (cm by default), so Blender's default unit scale/FBX scale method produces a factor of 100 (1 m exported as 100 cm units read as studs). Fix at source, not in Studio: in Blender keep Unit Scale 1.0 with 1 BU = 1 stud, apply scale/rotation (Ctrl+A) before export; in the FBX exporter use Path Mode Copy with Embed Textures on, Transform > Apply Scalings = FBX Unit Scale (or FBX All), Forward -Z / Up Y, Apply Unit on, Add Leaf Bones off, Bake Animation off unless exporting animation; and in the Studio 3D Importer check the scale/unit setting (Studs). GLB export avoids most unit issues.
G7: glTF/GLB exports mesh data, not Blender modifiers; with the exporter's Apply Modifiers option off it writes only the base cage, so the Mirror half never exists and Bevel geometry isn't generated. Fix: enable Include > Data > Mesh > Apply Modifiers (with UVs and Normals) or apply the modifiers manually. Catch: Apply Modifiers bakes the whole evaluated stack (including Subdivision, raising triangle count massively, and shape keys/armature interactions can break - modifiers plus shape keys may not export), and once applied manually you lose non-destructive editing - keep a source copy with live modifiers and export a baked duplicate. Set Mirror with Clipping/Merge and order Bevel after Mirror.
G8: 1) Scale on both axes ties width to screen width and height to screen height, so on different aspect ratios the frame's proportions change. Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (AspectRatio, AspectType FitWithinMaxSize/ScaleWithParentSize, DominantAxis), optionally UISizeConstraint min/max in pixels, or size one axis by scale and keep aspect. 2) The button is inside the unsafe area. Fix: set ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets (clears notch and Roblox top bar; DeviceSafeInsets clears only the notch, None only for full-screen background art), set SafeAreaCompatibility = None, keep IgnoreGuiInset false for interactive UI, and position with anchor/scale plus padding rather than hard-coding the top bar height (use GuiService.TopbarInset if needed, and react to changes).

local Items = require(game.ServerStorage.ItemConfig) -- {id = {price=..., maxQty=...}}
local last = {}
BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(plr, itemId, qty)
  local now = os.clock()
  if last[plr] and now - last[plr] < 0.25 then return end
  last[plr] = now
  if typeof(itemId) ~= 'string' or typeof(qty) ~= 'number' then return end
  if qty ~= qty or qty % 1 ~= 0 or qty < 1 or qty > 99 then return end
  local item = Items[itemId]
  if not item then return end
  local coins = plr:FindFirstChild('leaderstats') and plr.leaderstats:FindFirstChild('Coins')
  if not coins then return end
  local cost = item.price * qty -- price from server config only
  if coins.Value < cost then return end
  coins.Value -= cost
  Inventory.add(plr, itemId, qty) -- server-owned data, saved via session-locked store
end)
game.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```
Key points: never trust client price/amount, type/NaN/integer/range checks, whitelist ids, rate limit, deduct and grant atomically on the server.

-- key = 'u_'..userId, value = {lock={jobId=, time=}, data={...}}
function load(plr)
  for attempt = 1, 5 do
    local ok, res = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(plr), function(v)
      v = v or {data = defaultData()}
      if v.lock and v.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId and os.time() - v.lock.time < 1800 then
        return nil -- locked by another live server: cancel
      end
      v.lock = {jobId = game.JobId, time = os.time()}
      return v
    end)
    if ok and res and res.lock.jobId == game.JobId then return res.data end
    task.wait(attempt * 2) -- old server still saving: wait and retry
  end
  plr:Kick('Data busy, rejoin') -- never give a fresh profile on failure
end
function save(plr, release) -- autosave (refresh lock.time), PlayerRemoving, BindToClose
  store:UpdateAsync(key(plr), function(v)
    if not v or v.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId then return nil end -- lost lock: don't overwrite
    v.data = cache[plr]; v.lock = (not release) and {jobId=game.JobId, time=os.time()} or nil
    return v
  end)
end
```
Before TeleportAsync, save and release the lock (or the target waits for release). Track processed purchase/trade ids inside data so grants are idempotent; BindToClose saves all and waits.

T4: On the client, FireServer automatically passes the firing player as the first argument on the server. Passing LocalPlayer explicitly shifts the arguments: server receives (player, LocalPlayer, 50), so amount is the Player Instance and amount + 1 errors. Fix: client calls remote:FireServer(50). Server: remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, amount) if typeof(amount) ~= 'number' or amount ~= amount then return end print(amount + 1) end). Also never trust that amount - validate/clamp it on the server.
T5:
In Studio solo play the player can join before the server Script runs and connects PlayerAdded (the client loads fast and the script yields/requires first), so PlayerAdded never fires for that player. Standard fix: write a setup function, connect it, then loop over existing players:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local function onPlayerAdded(plr)
  local ls = Instance.new('Folder'); ls.Name = 'leaderstats'
  local c = Instance.new('IntValue'); c.Name = 'Coins'; c.Parent = ls
  ls.Parent = plr
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, plr in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, plr) end
```
Also connect before any yields (requires/WaitForChild) in the script.

T8: Your game almost certainly has Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs enabled (mesh streaming / cloud-generated LODs). In that mode Roblox generates and streams LODs itself and MeshPart.RenderFidelity is ignored (the property is slated for removal), so Precise does nothing and meshes still drop detail with distance. Options: accept the automatic LODs (they also save memory), check/adjust the Workspace setting, reduce reliance on distance detail by budgeting triangles at the source, or author your own LOD meshes and swap them. RenderFidelity only applies when that system is off.
